newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht falls, interbank steady to lower late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht falls, interbank steady to lower late.

text.p: Concerns over problems in the finance sector and commercial banks attempt to mop up ample liquidity in the system led to active selling of baht against the dollar late on Monday, dealers said.
Although the dollar was traded well above the mid-rate of 25.87 to the dollar late, the market was not exactly panicked, they said.

"The dollar also firmed up a bit against majors from the morning...The selling of the baht was active but not panicked. It is a far cry from a run on baht we saw early this year," said one dealer from a British bank here.
The baht was traded at 25.910-25.920 baht late Monday against 25.890-25.900 early.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted around 8.75-9.50 percent late compared with 9.00-9.50 percent in the morning.
The market was quiet. Commercial banks were flushed with liquidity but many chose to buy dollars instead of lending to the finance firms due to jitters over their financial status.
The interfinance rate was quoted between 12-18 percent as the liquidity remained tight.
Dealers said the joint Finance Ministry and Bank of Thailand's news conference on Monday on measures to help financial institutions barely helped the situation.
"The details for support measures was not clearly spelled out. Basically, it seemed they were there primarily to tell the market who are in trouble," said one finance firm executive.
"And that raised the questions on who will be the next. It worsened the sentiment and made it more difficult to get funds," he added.
